newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's centre-right to meet Thursday on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's centre-right to meet Thursday on budget.

text.p: The leaders of parties in Italy's centre-right Freedom Alliance coalition will hold a working lunch on Thursday to discuss the government's planned mini-budget, political sources said.
The meeting was due to take place at 1100 GMT.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government last week unveiled a controversial mini-budget designed to plug a hole in state accounts and ensure that Italy is a founder member of the European single currency at its 1999 launch.
The package, designed to raise 15.5 trillion lire in 1997, was condemned by Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi as a "sham that has no effect on the mechanisms of public spending."
One of the most contested measures in the mini-budget, which has to be approved by parliament, is a requirement for firms to pay taxes on huge severance payment funds two years early.
